paragraphs.source_en: In 1976, as part of the Bogota Declaration, eight equatorial nations claimed territorial rights to geostationary orbit, which by the nature of orbital mechanics is perpetually over their heads. Geostationary orbit is valuable, and the idea was that these less-developed nations ought to get paid rent by anyone using their space. But, although to this day the Colombian constitution asserts special rights to a slice of that orbit, the claim has largely been ignored by the international community. If the same claim had been made by the country with the most powerful military in history and the most advanced space launch technology, we suspect the newly installed “for rent” sign would have been taken a bit more seriously.
